# Marina New York City - Full Site Content

> Cinematic New York City stories, events, guides, photography, and creator work by Marina Kapler (@marina.newyorkcity).

Marina Kapler is a New York City content creator, photographer, and visual storyteller specializing in cinematic iPhone videography, brand storytelling, event coverage, and licensed NYC footage. She holds an official NYC MOME press pass.

## Top Picks This Week (November 2 to 8, 2026)

- **Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree Arrival** (Nov 7, 2026) - Rockefeller Plaza, Midtown, FREE. Watch the iconic tree arrive and be raised before the holiday crowds begin.
- **Candy Land NYC** (Opening November 2026) - 1335 Avenue of the Americas, Midtown (next to NY Hilton Midtown), FREE ENTRY (retail experience). The first immersive Candy Land retail experience in the US: walk the life-size board through the Candied Apple Orchard, Gummy Mountains and Lollipop Forest, ending at a graham-cracker Candy Castle.
- **Bank of America Winter Village at Bryant Park** (Oct 28 - Dec 31, 2026) - Bryant Park, Sixth Avenue between West 40th and 42nd Streets, Manhattan, Park and rink admission free; rentals and purchases extra. Holiday shops, free-admission ice rink and rinkside food hall. The full season continues to February 28, 2027.
- **The Rink at Rockefeller Center** (90th anniversary season) - Rockefeller Plaza, Midtown, Admission from $22; skate rental $12. Skate beneath the city skyline during the rink's special 90th anniversary season.
- **Canstruction at Brookfield Place** (Oct 30 - Nov 9, 2026) - Brookfield Place, 230 Vesey St, FREE. Architects and engineers build giant sculptures entirely from canned food, on display in the Winter Garden before the cans are donated to City Harvest.
- **Macy's Holiday Square** (Oct 31 - Dec 2, 2026) - Macy's Herald Square, lower level, FREE ENTRY. A 50,000-square-foot holiday market inside the flagship with 35+ local vendors including Eataly, Levain and Pearl River Mart, plus workshops and a Museum of Ice Cream Sprinkle Pool.
- **Gingerbread NYC: The Great Borough Bake-Off** (Nov 6 - Dec 31, 2026) - Museum of the City of New York, 1220 Fifth Avenue, Manhattan, Included with museum admission. Edible recreations of iconic New York buildings and places. Exhibition continues to January 18, 2027.
- **Rockefeller Center Holiday Chalets** (Nov 6 - Dec 31, 2026) - Rockefeller Plaza, Manhattan, Ticketed; price varies by package. Private heated chalets overlooking The Rink and, after December 2, the Christmas Tree. Run continues to January 2, 2027.
- **Central Park Fall Foliage** (Early November 2026) - The Ramble, Reservoir + North Woods, FREE. Catch some of Manhattan's richest late-season color along scenic walking routes.
- **Times Square Midnight Moment** (Nightly) - Times Square digital billboards, FREE. Watch the world's largest recurring digital public-art display take over the screens.

- Dates: Through Dec 6, 2026
- Time: During park hours
- Location: Madison Square Park, Flatiron
- Price: FREE

- Good for: Art lovers, walkers, families, visitors

- Dates: Nightly
- Time: 11:57 PM-midnight
- Location: Times Square digital billboards
- Price: FREE

### Clouds by Olaf Breuning

- Dates: Oct 17 - Dec 31, 2026
- Time: Outdoor public space; accessible daily
- Location: Broadway pedestrian plazas, West 39th to West 40th Streets, Manhattan
- Price: Free
- Six monumental cloud sculptures rising up to 33 feet above Midtown. Installation continues to March 2027.
- Good for: Public art
- More info: https://garmentdistrict.nyc/clouds

- Location: MoMA, 11 W 53rd St

### Na Mira: NO SMOKING at MoMA

- Dates: Nov 14, 2026 - Feb 15, 2027
- Time: During museum hours
- Location: MoMA Marie-Josee and Henry Kravis Studio, 11 W 53rd St, Manhattan
- Price: Included with museum admission
- Na Mira's first solo museum show in NYC: a newly commissioned media installation using radio frequencies, infrared heat and holography, drawing on Korean shamanism.
- Good for: Art lovers, immersive installations
- More info: https://www.moma.org/calendar/exhibitions/5869

## News and Press - Original Coverage and Press Releases

Full archive: https://marinanewyorkcity.com/news-and-press

### NYSE Announces 103rd Annual Christmas Tree Lighting

2026-11-02 - press release

The New York Stock Exchange has announced its 103rd Annual Christmas Tree Lighting, set for Thursday, December 3, 2026, from 3:30 to 6:30 PM on Wall and Broad Streets.

The NYSE announced the date this week. The free public celebration brings more than 35 vendors, holiday performances, and seasonal festivities to Wall and Broad Streets in the Financial District, with the tree lighting expected around 5:15 PM. The Exchange describes the event as an incredible community celebration that marks the start of the holiday season.

This year's tree comes from the Town of Beekman in upstate New York. In early October, Town Supervisor Laureen Abbatantuono confirmed that Beekman's tree would go to the New York Stock Exchange, not Rockefeller Center, ending days of speculation after the town first teased the news. The exact location of the tree is being kept private to protect the family's privacy.

The NYSE tree lighting tradition dates back to 1923, nearly a decade before Rockefeller Center's first tree, making it one of New York's oldest holiday traditions. The tree stands outside the Exchange's neoclassical building on Broad Street, a short walk from the Charging Bull and Fearless Girl statues.

### 53rd Village Halloween Parade Takes Over Sixth Avenue

2026-10-31 - original coverage

The 53rd Annual Village Halloween Parade marched up Sixth Avenue on Halloween night, with tens of thousands of costumed marchers, giant puppets, and the return of the legendary Thriller dance.

On Saturday, October 31, the 53rd Annual Village Halloween Parade stepped off at 7pm and marched north up Sixth Avenue from Canal Street to West 15th Street, under this year's theme, Body and Soul. Tens of thousands of costumed marchers joined hundreds of giant puppets and more than 50 bands, while an estimated two million spectators lined the avenue. Watching is free, and anyone in a costume can march.

This year's parade opened with Firehorse!, a new giant puppet commission from MacArthur fellow and master puppeteer Basil Twist, choreographed by Julie Atlas Muz. Performance artist Joey Arias served as Grand Marshal.

Marina filmed the parade from Sixth Avenue, including the Thriller dance moment that turns the street into a giant Michael Jackson music video every year, and cut the night into a full YouTube video.

### Candlelight Halloween Concert Lights Up the Vessel

2026-10-31 - original coverage

For one night only, the Vessel at Hudson Yards glowed with thousands of candles as the Highline String Quartet performed Halloween classics for a Candlelight concert presented by Fever.

On Halloween night, October 31, the Vessel at Hudson Yards hosted a one-night-only Candlelight concert presented by Fever. The Highline String Quartet performed Halloween classics, including Thriller by Michael Jackson, the Stranger Things theme, the Addams Family theme, and Ghostbusters, surrounded by thousands of flameless candles inside the Vessel's copper-toned structure.

The concert ran from 9 to 10pm, with doors at 8:15pm. Tickets were available exclusively through the Fever app and website, starting at $75.60, and were not sold on site.

Marina attended and filmed the concert, capturing the string performance glowing inside the Vessel.

[Instagram reel: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfNrP7HMgrU/]

### Rockefeller Center Reveals Its 2026 Christmas Tree

2026-10-26 - press release

A 76-foot Norway spruce from West Edmeston, New York, will be this year's Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree, arriving in Midtown on November 7 before the December 2 lighting.

Rockefeller Center announced the tree on Monday, October 26. The Norway spruce is about 75 years old, 50 feet wide, and weighs roughly 11 tons. It was donated by Rebecca Decker of West Edmeston, a small town in upstate New York, and found by Erik Pauze, Rockefeller Center's head gardener, who has chosen the tree for more than 30 years.

The tree will be cut on Thursday, November 5, and arrive at Rockefeller Plaza on Saturday, November 7. Its arrival is a public event this year, Meet the Tree Day 2026, back for its second year, with a holiday workshop from Care Bears and FAO Schwarz, meet-and-greets with six Care Bears characters, photo opportunities, and arts and crafts on the plaza.

Once it goes up, the tree will be dressed in more than 50,000 multicolored LED lights strung across five miles of wire, topped with the 900-pound Swarovski star designed by architect Daniel Libeskind. The star holds more than three million crystals across 70 spikes.

The lighting ceremony is Wednesday, December 2, broadcast live as Christmas in Rockefeller Center from 7 to 10pm. Performances begin around 8pm, the countdown starts at 9:57pm, and the lights switch on just before 10pm. Public viewing is free.

The tree stays on display through January 9, 2027. When it comes down, it will be milled into lumber and donated to Habitat for Humanity. The first tree went up in 1931, when construction workers pooled their money for a 20-foot balsam fir, and the first official lighting followed in 1933. The scaffolding is expected to come down before Thanksgiving, so the last days of November are the quiet window to see the tree fully decorated, star in place, before the lighting night crowds arrive.

[Instagram reel: https://www.instagram.com/p/De9IB1tDXnF/]

### Herald Square Holiday Fair Returns to Broadway

2026-10-26 - press release

The Herald Square Holiday Fair returns to Broadway between 32nd and 36th Streets on November 12, with a Christmas carousel, a virtual reality sleigh ride, a snow slide, and the Urbanspace holiday market.

The fair runs November 12, 2026, through January 3, 2027, across Herald Square and Greeley Square Park, on Broadway between 32nd and 36th Streets. Community Board 5 approved the fair on October 19, with conditions on crowd management, bike lane protection, sanitation, and fire safety.

Opening day brings the Christmas Carousel, the Magical Sleigh Ride, and the Snow Slide, open daily from 10am to 10pm and closed on Thanksgiving Day. The Magical Sleigh Ride is a virtual reality experience.

From December 2, the Market by Urbanspace joins the fair on the 34th to 36th Street side, open daily from 11am to 9pm through January 3, with returning holiday shop favorites, new vendors, food and treats from local vendors, and a warm cocktail bar. The Giant Rocking Horse photo op stands nearby, open daily from 10am to 10pm.

Macy's Holiday Square, the Urbanspace market beside the flagship store, runs alongside the fair, so the whole 34th Street corridor turns into one long holiday market for the season.

[Instagram reel: https://www.instagram.com/reel/De7PtFbM0ua/]

### Kinlaw's FALL RISK Takes Over Times Square Tonight

2026-10-13 - press release

Times Square Arts presents the New York City premiere of FALL RISK, a one-night-only performance by artist Kinlaw.

Tonight at 8pm, Kinlaw will be suspended 150 feet above Duffy Square, on Broadway between 46th and 47th Streets, in their most extreme and personal work yet.

Originally commissioned by Art Omi, FALL RISK centers on survival staged as monument, with a microphone amplifying the artist's breathing under extreme physical pressure high above the street.

Free and open to the public. Press inquiries: timessquarearts@culturalcounsel.com.

### 82nd Annual Columbus Day Parade Returns to Fifth Avenue

2026-10-12 - original coverage

Fifth Avenue turned into a river of red, white, and green as the Columbus Day Parade returned to Midtown Manhattan.

Fifth Avenue turned into a river of red, white, and green on Monday, October 12, as the 82nd Annual Columbus Day Parade marched from 47th to 72nd Street, back after last year's storm cancellation.

More than 100 groups joined the world's largest celebration of Italian American heritage, which this year honored 250 years of Italian contributions to America during the nation's 250th anniversary year. Grand Marshal Ray Dalio was represented on the route by his son Matt Dalio, joined by honorees Ambassador Leandro Rizzuto and Dr. Evelyn C. Granieri.

Marina filmed the parade from the route for a full-length YouTube video, from the bands warming up before the 11:30 AM step-off to the floats passing the red-carpet performance zone.

[YouTube video: https://youtu.be/KwnAr5iiQmU - 82nd Annual Columbus Day Parade on Fifth Avenue]

### The Rink at Rockefeller Center Celebrates 90 Years

2026-09-09 - press release

The Rink at Rockefeller Center returns October 10 for its 90th season with a reimagined skating experience.

New this year: an expanded Skate House and VIP Skate Lounge opening November 14, the Holiday Chalets presented by Balsam Hill returning November 6, and six new 90th Anniversary Lodges debuting November 20 for parties up to eight guests.

Tickets start at $22 per person (rentals not included) and are on sale now at rockefellercenter.com.

Built as a temporary attraction in 1936, The Rink now welcomes more than a quarter of a million skaters each year.

## About

Marina Kapler films New York like she never got used to it. Her work covers NYC neighborhoods, seasonal events, skylines, observation decks, and exact landmark locations, shot cinematically on iPhone. She covers parades, holiday markets, tree lightings, rink openings, and major city events, and licenses her footage to media outlets.
